coverage.reason: Existing native viewer controls are retained.
No stored preferences or gameplay state change.
Only local same-origin authored GLB assets are loaded; no auth changes.
Reactions consume the actual bounded presented projectile stream and remote player poses without adding protocol messages.
Packed GLBs load alongside city preparation, shaders/buffers warm before play, and distant cameos skip animation work.
No controls, interface cues, text, sound or input changes; existing optional game character acting is preserved.
Compare original geometry, animation samples and GLB resource sizes.
Use established Three.js GLTF loading and keyframe optimization.

direct.name: three
direct.compatibility: Existing locked Three.js 0.182.0 and matching addons. No added dependencies.
direct.ownership: CameoView owns cosmetic reactions and bounded state; GameSession supplies current rats and rendered ball samples; existing CheeseGun spatial index checks scenery. createGame owns preload and GPU preparation. Server physics, damage and scores are unchanged.

behavior.behavior: Load GLB assets with existing GLTFLoader; retain their scene hierarchy and animation. KeyframeTrack.optimize removes redundant constant keys.
behavior.do_not_copy: Do not copy example styling, environment textures or camera. Preserve accepted characters and silent art scope.

platform.requirement: compileAsync prepares materials using parallel shader compilation when supported. Yield before initial upload; no guaranteed device FPS claim.

proof: Run npx vitest run --config vitest.client.config.ts test/client/cameoView.test.ts test/client/cameoLoading.test.ts test/client/cameoAnimations.test.ts test/client/session.test.ts
Run npm run typecheck for application and test types.
Run npm test for Worker, client and script regressions.
Run npm run build for the complete production client.
Inspect both actual-city placements in test/visual/cameo-placement.html using static cameras.
